name: eiswolfs-flightradar-CYD
description: Live ADS-B flight radar for the Cheap Yellow Display (CYD / ESP32-2432S028) - radar sweep, aircraft silhouettes, weather effects, web UI, MQTT & more

paragraphs: A live ADS-B flight radar running on the ESP32 "Cheap Yellow Display" (CYD, ESP32-2432S028), showing nearby aircraft on a rotating radar screen with altitude/speed/model/route details and a proximity LED alert.
features: The main screen is a circular radar view, sized to the full screen width, with a rotating sweep line and a twinkling starfield filling the space outside the radar circle. Each aircraft marker shows a recognizable type…

Every visible aircraft also gets a small triangular chevron just above or below its marker showing whether it's currently climbing or descending (derived from the same vertical rate already used for the Climb/Descent…

Aircraft are color-coded by altitude - green below 10,000 ft, yellow between 10,000-30,000 ft, red above 30,000 ft - with a legend at the bottom of the radar screen. Tapping the legend opens a full-screen overlay…

Color themes & effects: under Menu → System → "Radar Display", the "Colors" button switches between five color themes - Green, Amber, Blue, Red, or Purple - applied system-wide (menus, buttons, borders, text); aircraft…

whatItDoes.text: A live ADS-B flight radar running on the ESP32 "Cheap Yellow Display" (CYD, ESP32-2432S028), showing nearby aircraft on a rotating radar screen with altitude/speed/model/route details and a proximity LED alert.

requirements.text: Turn it on, enter your broker's address (host and port, e.g. 192.168.1.10:1883), and optionally a username/password if your broker requires authentication - public test brokers without a login work too.

An optional push-notification integration (Menu → System → Tools → "ntfy.sh Push", off by default) sends a notification straight to your phone via the free ntfy.sh service whenever an emergency squawk or a watchlist match is detected - no account or server of your own needed, just install the free ntfy app (or use a browser) and subscribe to a topic name of your choosing.
Powered by the free Open-Meteo API (no API key needed), refreshed automatically every 5 minutes or immediately after switching location.
